text:
maria-g: heads up — after the v2.3.1 rollout to canary yesterday we saw a ~35% p95 jump for a small cohort (cohort: tenant-44). customer support just flagged two complaints. :frowning:
ajay: ok can you paste the cohort query and sample traces? any p99 change?
sophia: p99 flat, it's specifically p95 that moved from ~180ms to ~240ms on the canary hosts. baseline hosts unchanged.
maria-g: sample perf graph: https://redwood-grafana/graph?panelId=78&from=8165400000&to=8165430000 (look at tenant-44 overlay). also attached a small flame for a 220ms request.
nate: any config differences in the canary? kernel, allocator, scheduler flags?
maria-g: same flags AFAIK; this was a rollforward that included the new local-scheduler change + jemalloc bump.
sophia: hypothesis 1: local-scheduler interacts with auth refresh fanout causing brief micro-queueing for mid-latency requests. hypothesis 2: jemalloc bump changed fragmentation -> small latency bump under modest concurrency.
ajay: can we repro with synthetic replay against canary? if we can reproduce we can bisect between the scheduler change and jemalloc change.
customer-support: we have 2 affected customers, both reported UI lag around 10:30 PST, small % of requests. they want ETA.
maria-g: working on repro. running a replay job now with tenant-44 trace sample at production QPS.
( deploy-bot ): replay job r-2026-03-17-08 started on canary pool-3, id r-9876 :rocket:
sophia: while replay runs, get heap / allocator metrics from the canary pods and baseline. also KV cache hit rate during those spans.
ajay: quick check — is KV cache colder on canary because of new binary path? samples show some cold sequences in tail.
elena: I pulled one trace: there is a 30ms stall inside scheduler.work_loop when requests queue hits 7, then burst of redis calls. attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T10:30:21Z] scheduler.work_loop: wait(7) -> dispatch
[2026-03-17T10:30:21Z] auth.fetch_token: 120ms
[2026-03-17T10:30:21Z] model.kv.get: 6ms
```
nate: auth.fetch_token at 120ms is suspicious — is auth service under load or sync fetch introduced?
maria-g: auth service healthy; but the canary host shows increased synchronous permfetchs per request. might be a path that forgot async permcache.
sophia: if permfetch became sync for some code path, that would move many mid-tail requests up. we should look for the change in the rollforward diff.
ajay: agreed. I'll run a quick git-bisect across the two commits (scheduler change vs jemalloc bump) using a lightweight synthetic that stresses mid-latency region.
( deploy-bot ): bisect job b-424 queued, estimated 12m.
maria-g: meanwhile mitigation options: 1) route tenant-44 away from canary (traffic-slew) 2) temporary rollback of scheduler change 3) patch to make permfetch async fallback.
customer-support: prefer routing for now, customers want minimal disruption.
ajay: can do traffic-slew for tenant-44 to baseline cluster. I'll run a 50% -> 100% in 5m steps.
( deploy-bot ): traffic-slew applied: tenant-44 50%->baseline at 8165432050 :white_check_mark:
elena: after 10m post-slew p95 for tenant-44 back to ~182ms on baseline. canary still shows 240ms for other tenants with similar access patterns.
sophia: ok that tells us it's likely canary-local change, not jemalloc global. bisect results will confirm which PR introduced sync permfetch.
ajay: bisect finished — culprit: commit 5c7a2b0 toggled a fast-path in scheduler that removed an async permcache check.
maria-g: can we hotfix that to re-enable async permcache in the scheduler fast-path?
ajay: yes, PR ready, tests pass. will hotpatch to the canary hosts and monitor.
( deploy-bot ): hotpatch h-2026-03-17 applied to canary pool-3 at 8165432150 :rocket:
elena: after hotpatch p95 fell from 240ms -> 188ms within two minutes for tenant-44. p99 unchanged.
maria-g: great. notify customers and mark incident as mitigated. next steps: include the permcache async check in the rollout checklist and add a synthetic mid-tail probe to CI that mirrors tenant-44 QPS pattern.
sophia: also add a dashboard alert for cohort-specific p95 deltas >15% vs baseline for 30m.
nate: i'll open a follow-up ticket for jemalloc tuning investigation separate from this fix.
customer-support: thanks team — I'll update customers and close escalation after confirmation window (30m). :thumbsup:
maria-g: thanks all, leaving notes in the rollout doc and adding the bisect commands to the playbook for future.
